SPARK uses that agreement as related support for extreme-weather/emergency-management and flood-survey projects; neither project describes lightning calibration or this output. No positive project-specific bridge in the examined authoritative sources.
attribution_followups_rechecked.question: Is there direct documentation that this lightning-HREF work was a deliverable of one of the named WPO survey projects?

attribution_followups_rechecked.output: Initialization of upper ocean temperature towards forecast improvements in GFSv17
attribution_followups_rechecked.finding: The NCEP Office Note concerns SST initialization and GFSv17; source lists NESDIS CI awards NA19NES4320002 and NA24NESX432C0001. SPARK references NA19NES4320002 only as a related award to a JTTI project on particle-filter non-Gaussian global data assimilation. Shared UFS/GFS terminology is not proof of the project workstream.
attribution_followups_rechecked.question: Is this GFSv17 SST initialization office note directly listed as a product of WPO NA23OAR4590379?

attribution_followups_rechecked.output: The FireHouse 1.0: Unified end-user insights on fire weather
attribution_followups_rechecked.finding: NOAA IR attributes the report to GSL/CIRA Fire Weather Testbed and lists multiple NOAA awards. NOAA GSL describes Fire Weather Testbed as a separate fire-management effort. SPARK links the broad CI award as related to a tropical-cyclone AI forecast project; no specific deliverable bridge.
attribution_followups_rechecked.question: Does a primary WPO project report link FireHouse to the tropical-cyclone AI workstream rather than independent fire-weather testbed activity?
